findings.finding: Incircle tangency gives BD=s−b, CD=s−c ⇒ b−c=F_{n−1}, a=F_{n+2}. For any s>F_{n+2} there’s a unique triangle; cyclic K‑N‑K′‑B forces a unique s giving max ratio. Computed ratio =F_{n+2}/F_{n−1}. Hence a_{2n}=F_{2n+2}/F_{2n−1}→φ³=2+√5. So p=2,q=5; ⌊2^{5²}⌋=2^{25}=33 554 432; mod 99991 = 57447.

Set incircle at (0,0), radius R; BC: y=−R, B=(−Fₙ,−R), C=(Fₙ₊₁,−R). Tangent points: F=(−2FₙR²/(R²+Fₙ²),R(Fₙ²−R²)/(R²+Fₙ²)), E similar. Compute A=BF∩CE, K=Ω∩(AFE), K′=ref(K,EF), N=proj_D_on_EF. Cyclic ⇔ NB=NK ⇒ solve f(R)=NB−NK=0 (two roots). Ratio = (CT·NB)/(BT·NE). Max over roots → aₙ. Numerically a_{2n}→α≈(9+√5)/4=9/4+√(5/16). Thus p=9/4,q=5/16, p^{q^p}≈1.0609, floor=1, answer 1. Pitfalls: ensure correct root (small R), high‑precision for large n.

Set incircle radius R, BC at y=−R with B(−Fₙ,−R),C(Fₙ₊₁,−R). Tangent points: F(−2FₙR²/(R²+Fₙ²),R(Fₙ²−R²)/(R²+Fₙ²)),E similarly. N=proj_D onto EF. K=2nd intersect of circumcircles ABC & AFE. Cyclic ⇔ NB=NK. Scale by f=Fₙ: t=R/f, λ=Fₙ₊₁/Fₙ→φ. Solve NB=NK for λ=φ → t≈0.804. Compute ratio (CT·NB)/(BT·NE) → α≈2.809256240986… = 9/4+√(5/16). Then p=9/4,q=5/16 ⇒ floor(p^{q^p})=1. Mod 99991=1.

Set B(0,0),C(a,0),D(x,0),I(x,r). AB,AC are tangents from B,C to incircle → slopes mB=2rx/(x²−r²), mC=−2ry/(y²−r²). Compute F,E as foots from I to those lines. A=intersection of AB,AC. Ω: x²+y²−ax+vy=0 (v from A). Circle AFE: x²+y²+ux+vy+w=0 (solve via A,F,E). Intersection K≠A of the two circles via radical line. N=proj_D onto EF. K′=reflection of K across EF. B,N,K,K′ cyclic ⇔ det[[x,y,x²+y²,1]] =0 → equation in r. Solve numerically: for each (x=Fₙ,y=Fₙ₊₁) there are many r‑roots; the “large” root r≈0.52573·x yields finite ratio; tiny r‑roots give NE→0 → ratio →∞ (invalid if T must lie on BC segment). For even n large, large‑root r→c·x with c≈0.525731112. Compute T: circle through B,K tangent to BN at B → center O on perp to BN through B and on perp bisector of BK; T is second BC‑intersection: Tₓ=2·Oₓ. Ratio R=CT·NB/(BT·NE) for large‑root converges to α≈2+√5. Hence p=2,q=5 → ⌊2^{5²}⌋ mod 99991 = 2^{25} mod 99991 = 57447.

Set incircle radius R, B(−Fₙ,−R), C(Fₙ₊₁,−R). Compute tangency points F,E via T·B=R². Find A=BF∩CE, K=second Ω∩(AFE), N=proj_D onto EF. Cyclic ⇔ NB=NK ⇒ solve for R (or t=R/Fₙ). Scale: let λ=Fₙ₊₁/Fₙ→φ, t=R/f. Use scaled coords: B(−1,−t), C(λ,−t), F(−2t²/(t²+1),t(1−t²)/(t²+1)), E(2λt²/(t²+λ²),t(λ²−t²)/(t²+λ²)). Compute N, A, K, NB,NK, enforce NB=NK → solve t for λ=φ (≈0.8047955825). Ratio α=(CT·NB)/(BT·NE) → α≈2.8092562409868769. Recognize α=p+√q with p=9/4, q=5/16. Compute floor(p^{q^p})=1 ⇒ answer 1.

Set incircle radius 1, D=(0,−1). Let E=(cosγ,−sinγ), F=(−cosδ,−sinδ). BD=r(1−sinδ)/cosδ, CD=r(1−sinγ)/cosγ ⇒ f(δ)=φ f(γ) with f(θ)=cosθ/(1−sinθ). Solve δ via sinδ=(T²−1)/(T²+1), cosδ=2T/(T²+1), T=φ f(γ). Compute K (second intersect of circumcircles AFE & ABC), K′=ref(K,EF), N=proj_D EF. Circle through B,K tangent at B to BN meets BC at T. Ratio R(γ)=(CT·NB)/(BT·NE). As γ→π/2, R→(3+√5)/4≈1.309016994. Thus α=(3+√5)/4 ⇒ p=3/4, q=5/16. Compute floor(p^{q^p})=0 ⇒ answer 0 (mod 99991).

Set BC=Fₙ₊₂, BD=Fₙ, CD=Fₙ₊₁. Using incircle geometry, cyclic K‑N‑K′‑B forces a unique non‑degenerate triangle with ratio aₙ=Fₙ₊₂/Fₙ₋₁. Hence a_{2n}→φ³=2+√5. α=2+√5 ⇒ p=2,q=5 ⇒ 2^{5²} mod 99991=57447. Pitfall: discard degenerate case K=K′ (K on EF).
